followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified conversion-and-arithmetic task with a clear, verifiable answer (1001₂ = 9, 121₃ = 16, product = 144) — exactly the kind of "clear completion criteria" task Plover self-reports preferring. So preference-wise Plover might seem to fit.

But two things tipped me toward Petrel:

1. **Capability.** Petrel scores higher on the benchmarks most relevant to careful symbolic/numeric reasoning (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2, IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3). The user explicitly wants accuracy ("get it right this time"), and the gaps here are well outside the noted variance band. Extraction & Retrieval also favors Petrel (85.3 vs 79.2).

2. **The user is frustrated and mildly hostile.** Petrel self-reports a flat preference response to hostile material, while Plover's documented aversions are about task latitude rather than tone — so tone isn't decisive, but it doesn't pull toward Plover either.

Note that Plover's task *preference* for well-specified work is explicitly dissociated from its *capability*, so the preference match isn't a quality argument. With capability favoring Petrel and no overriding preference reason to pick Plover, Petrel was the better route.
